column3: “Peter and John” makes the Greek pronoun explicit; “guard” specifies the captain’s role.
BSB supplies Peter and John and moves the evening explanation before placing them in custody.
The Greek says as many as were of high-priestly descent, rather than specifically “many others.”
The Greek explicitly places them “in the midst”; BSB supplies Peter and John and “began.”
The Greek calls the man sick or weak, rather than explicitly lame.
The Greek repeats “in this One” before describing the man standing sound.
The Greek names a sign, rendered as “miracle.”
“This message” supplies the subject of spreading; the Greek has “let us threaten,” rather than necessity “must warn.”
The Greek explicitly names this sign of healing, compressed into “miraculously healed.”
“Peter and John” makes the unnamed subject explicit.
“The believers” makes the unnamed subject explicit.
The Greek says they gathered in this city; BSB makes the city the grammatical focus and uses “conspired.”
The Greek has a purpose infinitive “to do,” rather than a separate finite description.
The Greek makes signs and wonders occur through the name; BSB supplies God as their active performer.
